newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares closed higher on Tuesday, squeezed by options-related short-covering with sentiment further boosted by strong gains in companies which have recently reported results, dealers said.
"The big story today is Nutricia which just keeps going up and up and up," said one dealer. "People are still piling in because they're afraid of getting left behind," he added.

The AEX index closed up 4.22 points at 560.41. "There's been a big move out of the options market to cover shorts, and with relatively modest volumes it only takes that to push the index up by this much," said another dealer.
"It's not all that broadly based," another dealer said. "All it's taken today is a few big climbers like Nutricia and Wolters Kluwer to make people feel good about the market."
Others said today's gains could prove fragile, with a lacklustre dollar and bonds giving scant grounds to push the market ahead after recent weakness.

"Why should you buy these stocks now when you could get them a lot cheaper yesterday?" said a dealer. "But when stocks like Aegon are a few guilders higher then you will see the index respond -- other than that there's no real reason for the market to be moving like this," he said.

Nutricia closed 9.60 guilders or 4.5 percent higher at 223.70, still pushing up after Thursday's announcement of a 51 percent jump in half year profit. The shares have come up from around 191 since Thursday.

Aegon found fresh buyers, rising 2.10 guilders to 91.70 in response to its results also last week, although Dutch PTT sagged 20 cents to 58.50 guilders, still overshadowed by first half results on Friday which disappointed most expectations.
Food ingredients and biotechnology firm Gist Brocades excited early interest, reaching a day's peak of 57.70 ahead of results on Thursday, before closing up 1.10 at 56.90 guilders.
Dealers said Wolters Kluwer was drawing attention as a potential growth stock, pushing the shares 6.80 guilders higher to 213.80 guilders.

Shares in fellow publisher VNU closed 0.40 guilders up at 29.10, just before news first half net from ordinary operations rose to 143 million guilders from a previous 126 million, well within the 132 to 148 million analysts' forecast range.
Leading internationals were mostly firm with Unilever up 1.49 guilders to 240.90 and Philips 70 cents harder at 56.80 guilders, although Royal Dutch dipped 1.30 guilders to 251.00.
